paragraphs.title: The Strengthening of David’s Kingdom and His Ties with Tyre

easy.explanation: Hiram king of Tyre sent these men and materials to David.
easy.q: Who sent messengers, cedar timber, masons, and carpenters to David?

answers: To build a wall around Tyre
easy.explanation: They were sent to build David an house.
easy.q: What were the cedar timber and craftsmen sent to David for?

answers: That it was about to become weak
That the LORD had confirmed him king and lifted up his kingdom
easy.explanation: David perceived that the LORD had confirmed him king and lifted up his kingdom.
easy.q: What did David perceive about his kingdom?

answers: He helped David build an house
He gave his kingdom to David
medium.explanation: Hiram supplied timber and skilled workers for David’s house.
medium.q: How did Hiram’s actions help David?

answers: His kingdom was hidden from the nations
His kingdom was exalted and strengthened
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the rising strength and prominence of David’s kingdom.
medium.q: What does “his kingdom was lifted up on high” mean?

answers: Because he had recruited the Philistines
Because the LORD had confirmed him king over Israel
medium.explanation: David attributed his royal authority and success to the LORD.
medium.q: Why did David understand that his kingdom had been strengthened?

answers: David had friendly cooperation with a foreign king
challenge.explanation: The gift of materials and craftsmen shows cooperation between Hiram and David.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Hiram sending builders to David?

answers: The kingdom was only for David personally
David’s exaltation was connected with the good of Israel
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the lifting up of David’s kingdom with his people Israel.
challenge.q: What does “because of his people Israel” emphasize?

answers: Help in building a house, the strengthening of the kingdom, and Israel’s exaltation
Leaving Tyre, the fall of the kingdom, and building a house
challenge.explanation: Hiram first sends building help, and David then recognizes the LORD’s blessing on his kingdom and people.
challenge.q: What sequence is described in these verses?

easy.explanation: The verse says that David took more wives at Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where did David take more wives?

easy.explanation: David begat more sons and daughters in Jerusalem.
easy.q: What did David beget in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: Solomon is one of the children named in the passage.
easy.q: Which name appears in the list of David’s children?

answers: They were born to David in Jerusalem
They were all kings of Tyre
medium.explanation: The passage introduces them as David’s children in Jerusalem.
medium.q: What do the children named in these verses have in common?

medium.explanation: The list names Nathan and Solomon together.
medium.q: Which name appears after Nathan in the list?
How many children’s names are listed in these verses?

answers: The passage moves from the family event to the children who resulted from it
The children were sent to Tyre
challenge.explanation: The verses first mention David’s additional wives and then give the names of his children.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the movement from David’s marriages to the list of names?

challenge.explanation: Elishama and Beeliada are named together near the end of the list.
challenge.q: Which pair of names appears together in the passage?

challenge.explanation: The passage says David took more wives at Jerusalem but does not give their number.
challenge.q: What is not stated about David’s additional wives?

paragraphs.title: The First Conflict with the Philistines

easy.explanation: The Philistines went up to seek David.
easy.q: Who went up to seek David after hearing that he was anointed king?

easy.explanation: They spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
easy.q: Where did the Philistines spread themselves?

easy.explanation: David asked God whether he should go up against the Philistines.
easy.q: What did David do before going against the Philistines?

answers: Do not go up after them
Go up; for I will deliver them into thine hand
Wait for the sound of going
medium.explanation: The LORD told David to go up and promised to deliver the Philistines into his hand.
medium.q: What was the LORD’s answer to David’s first enquiry?

answers: God broke in upon David’s enemies like the breaking forth of waters
The Philistines broke into David’s camp
medium.explanation: David said that God had broken in upon his enemies like waters breaking forth.
medium.q: Why was the place called Baal-perazim?

answers: They buried them in the valley
medium.explanation: The Philistines left their gods behind, and David commanded that they be burned.
medium.q: What did the Philistines do with their gods after they were smitten?

answers: He went out against them and enquired of God
He asked Hiram for an army
challenge.explanation: David went out against them and sought God’s direction.
challenge.q: What did David do after learning that the Philistines had come against him?

answers: The Philistines were defeated and left their gods behind
David adopted the gods of the Philistines
challenge.explanation: The abandoned idols and their burning follow the Philistines’ defeat.
challenge.q: What does the burning of the idols show about the battle’s result?

answers: The Philistines came, David asked God, and God gave him a command
David burned the idols, so the Philistines began the war
Hiram sent builders, so the Philistines left their gods
challenge.explanation: The Philistines’ arrival led David to enquire of God, who directed him to battle.
challenge.q: Which cause-and-effect sequence appears in the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Second Victory and the Spread of David’s Fame

answers: They spread themselves abroad in the valley again
easy.explanation: The Philistines yet again spread themselves abroad in the valley.
easy.q: What did the Philistines do after the first battle?

answers: Turn away from them and come upon them over against the mulberry trees
easy.explanation: God told David to turn away and approach them over against the mulberry trees.
easy.q: What did God command David to do in the second battle?

easy.explanation: The verse says they smote the host from Gibeon even to Gazer.
easy.q: How far did David’s forces smite the Philistines?

answers: A sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees
medium.explanation: God told David to go out when he heard the sound of going in the mulberry trees.
medium.q: What sign was David to wait for before going to battle?

answers: Circle around the enemy rather than attack directly
medium.explanation: David was instructed to approach from another direction instead of going directly after them.
medium.q: What does “turn away from them” mean in this context?

answers: He did as God commanded him
medium.q: What did David do after receiving the command?

answers: That David’s action depended on a divine sign and instruction
That David did not know who the enemy was
challenge.explanation: David was to wait for the appointed sign before going out to battle.
challenge.q: What does the sound before the battle emphasize?

answers: God was leading the battle before David
The Philistines went ahead of David to flee
challenge.explanation: The verse presents God as going before David to smite the Philistine host.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the words “God is gone forth before thee”?

answers: David’s fame spread into all lands, and the LORD brought fear of him upon the nations
challenge.explanation: After the victory, David’s fame spread and the LORD brought fear of him upon the nations.
challenge.q: What was the result of the second victory?
